meta.project: Integrated ESG-ABSA Intelligence Framework (v-1 to v3)
meta.description: Comprehensive reference mapping linking integrated research layers to technical contributions, research questions, and supporting literature evidence from the NAACL-2025 and thesis evaluation corpus.

research_questions: RQ1.1: How can Transformer-based architectures be optimized for bilingual ESG ABSA?
RQ1.3: How can regional calibration and ESG lexicons mitigate bias?

literature_references.title: Improving Informally Romanized Language Identification
literature_references.authors: Adrian Benton, Alexander Gutkin, Christo Kirov, Brian Roark
literature_references.relevance: Supports C3 and RQ1.1 by demonstrating that training on synthetic data capturing natural spelling variations improves identification in romanized text, validating strategies for handling multilingual variability in non-Latin scripts such as Indonesian.

literature_references.title: P-MMEval: A Parallel Multilingual Multitask Benchmark for Consistent Evaluation of LLMs
literature_references.authors: Boyi Deng, Fei Huang, et al.
literature_references.relevance: Directly supports C1 and C9 by providing a large-scale benchmark for consistent evaluation across diverse languages and tasks, establishing the necessary baselines for a bilingual platform.

contributions: C8: Large-scale ESG LLM benchmark (30+ models)
research_questions: RQ2.1: To what extent does few-shot learning improve ESG granularity?
RQ2.4: How can multi-LLM fusion reduce hallucination?
RQ2.2: How can long-context mechanisms enhance scalability?

literature_references.title: Comparing Specialised Small and General Large Language Models on Text Classification: 100 Labelled Samples to Achieve Break-Even Performance
literature_references.authors: Branislav Pecher, Ivan Srba, M. Bieliková
literature_references.relevance: Justifies C16 and RQ2.1 by proving that specialized models require only approximately 100 samples to match general models in specific domains, validating the few-shot granularity hypothesis.

literature_references.title: E2LLM: Encoder Elongated Large Language Models for Long-Context Understanding and Reasoning
literature_references.authors: Zihan Liao, Jun Wang, et al.
literature_references.relevance: Supports C13 and RQ2.2 by presenting a method to compress long contexts into soft prompts using pretrained encoders, enabling efficient and scalable long-context processing.

literature_references.title: Mixture-of-Clustered-Experts: Advancing Expert Specialization and Generalization in Instruction Tuning
literature_references.authors: Sugyeong Eo, Jungjun Lee, et al.
literature_references.relevance: Provides the architectural logic for C10 and RQ2.4, demonstrating that dual-stage routing based on input heterogeneity improves specialization and robustness, reducing hallucination risks.

research_questions: RQ3.1: How can symbolic reasoning be integrated using ESG ontologies?
RQ3.2: How can transparent outputs be ensured via reasoning graphs?
RQ3.3: How can implicit ESG claims be identified?

literature_references.title: FLARE: Faithful Logic-Aided Reasoning and Exploration
literature_references.authors: Erik Arakelyan, Pasquale Minervini, et al.
literature_references.relevance: Causally links to C7 and RQ3.1 by soft-formalizing queries into logic programming and using multi-hop search to ensure reasoning faithfulness and transparency.

literature_references.title: DEL-ToM: Inference-Time Scaling for Theory-of-Mind Reasoning via Dynamic Epistemic Logic
literature_references.relevance: Supports C7 and RQ3.1 by proposing a framework for structured and transparent reasoning grounded in Dynamic Epistemic Logic, facilitating verifiable reasoning traces.

literature_references.title: TaxoAlign: Scholarly Taxonomy Generation Using Language Models
literature_references.authors: Avishek Lahiri, Yufang Hou, et al.
literature_references.relevance: Direct evidence for C15 and RQ3.1, offering a framework for generating and aligning complex taxonomies to enforce semantic coherence with expert structures.

research_questions: RQ4.1: How can XAI improve stakeholder trust in ESG outputs?
RQ4.5: Can tone–outcome mismatch reliably indicate greenwashing?

literature_references.title: The Missing Parts: Augmenting Fact Verification with Half Truth Detection
literature_references.authors: Yixuan Tang, Anthony K. H. Tung, et al.
literature_references.relevance: Directly supports C11 and RQ4.5 by identifying omission-based misinformation (half-truths), which is a core indicator for quantitative greenwashing risk.

literature_references.title: A Symbolic Adversarial Learning Framework for Evolving Fake News Generation and Detection
literature_references.authors: Xiuying Chen, Qirong Ho, et al.
literature_references.relevance: Operationalizes RQ4.5 by using structured agent debates to identify logical and factual flaws in deceptive narratives, mirroring the proposed tone-action-outcome mismatch scoring.

literature_references.title: DRES: Fake news detection by dynamic representation and ensemble selection
literature_references.authors: Faramarz Farhangian, L. A. Ensina, et al.
literature_references.relevance: Supports C11 and RQ4.5 by leveraging instance hardness to detect difficult misinformation cases, providing a proxy for identifying sophisticated greenwashing claims.

research_questions: RQ5.1: How can transparent and auditable outputs be ensured?
RQ5.2: How can reasoning quality and consistency be operationalized at scale?

literature_references.title: CheckEval: A reliable LLM-as-a-Judge framework for evaluating text generation using checklists
literature_references.authors: Yukyung Lee, Joonghoon Kim, et al.
literature_references.relevance: Provides the methodological basis for C5 and RQ5.1 by enabling interpretable, traceable binary decisions in evaluation pipelines, ensuring auditable system outputs.

literature_references.title: LMR-BENCH: Evaluating LLM Agent's Ability on Reproducing Language Modeling Research
literature_references.authors: Shuo Yan, Ruochen Li, et al.
literature_references.relevance: Supports C12 and RQ5.2 by establishing a benchmark for the autonomous reproduction of research code, essential for the open-source and reproducibility goals of Objective 5.

literature_references.title: A Systematic Survey of Automatic Prompt Optimization Techniques
literature_references.authors: Lin Cheong, Han Ding, et al.
literature_references.relevance: Justifies the automation and scalability goals of C12 and RQ5.2 by summarizing best practices for prompt optimization in production environments.
